# Plan: `index.html` — 3D Space Shooter (single file)

## 1. Tech & delivery
- **One file**: `/tmp/ocb/task-2-asteroid-run/mimo-v2.6-flash/index.html` — inline CSS + inline JS, no external assets except Three.js.
- **Three.js loading**: classic `<script src>` UMD build (`cdnjs .../r128/three.min.js`, global `THREE`) with `onerror` fallback to a second CDN (`unpkg three@0.152.2/build/three.min.js`). Classic script tags work under `file://` without CORS issues; if both fail, show a plain-text error overlay.
- **No fonts/textures/models** — all geometry from Three.js primitives, HUD is DOM text with system fonts.

## 2. Gameplay model (camera & space)
Tunnel-style shooter (readable, playable, and easy to autopilot):
- Ship lives on a play plane at `z = 0`, bounded box `x ∈ [-40, 40]`, `y ∈ [-24, 24]`.
- Camera sits behind/above at `z ≈ 22`, slight follow-lag + tilt for juice; looks down −Z.
- Asteroids spawn at `z ≈ -320`, drift toward the player (+Z) with lateral spin/drift; they despawn past the camera (passing the ship = 1 life lost).
- Player bolts travel along −Z. Sphere-sphere collisions for bolt↔asteroid and ship↔asteroid.

## 3. Entities
- **Ship**: group of primitives (elongated octahedron/cone fuselage, swept box wings, glowing engine sphere) + thruster light; bank/tilt animation from velocity; invulnerability blink after a hit.
- **Asteroids**: shared `IcosahedronGeometry` per tier (detail 1) with randomized vertex displacement for craggy silhouettes; 3 tiers (big/med/small), tinted gray-brown, slow tumble. **Shot big → 2 medium → 2 small → destroyed**; score `20 / 50 / 100`.
- **Bullets**: pooled glowing capsules (emissive) with a small point-glow sprite; fire cooldown ~150 ms, hold Space to autofire.
- **Explosion particles**: pooled `THREE.Points` (~2000) with a tiny custom `ShaderMaterial` — per-particle size, color, life-fade, additive blending, `depthWrite:false`. Emitters sized by explosion tier; plus a brief expanding glow ring/flash mesh for big hits.
- **Starfield**: two static `THREE.Points` shells (near/far) for parallax; `THREE.Fog` for depth; dark blue-black background.

## 4. Audio (Web Audio API only)
`AudioContext` created/resumed on the **first user gesture** (keydown/click) to satisfy autoplay policy; attract mode runs silently until then (correct per spec — no input needed to start).
- `laser`: fast downward sawtooth sweep + short envelope.
- `explosion(size)`: white-noise buffer through lowpass sweep, decay scaled by tier.
- `damage`: low square-wave thud + noise.
- `gameOver`: descending arpeggio; `restart`/`lifeUp`: bright blip.
- Master `GainNode` with simple limiter; all nodes stopped/disconnect on end (no leaks).

## 5. State machine & modes
```
ATTRACT  → (any key) → PLAYING → (lives 0) → GAMEOVER → (Space/R or 6s auto) → ATTRACT
```
- **Boots directly into ATTRACT** with autopilot engaged — plays immediately, zero input.
- **Idle rule**: `lastInputTime` updated on every keydown/mouse event; if `now - lastInput > 3000 ms` → autopilot takes over (smooth handoff: AI writes the same virtual inputs the keyboard would). Any input instantly returns control.
- **HUD** (DOM overlay): score, high score (session), lives icons, wave, state banner ("ATTRACT MODE — press any key", "GAME OVER", pause hint), center crosshair. Blinking "AUTOPilot" indicator when AI drives.
- **Game over**: slow-mo/freeze frame, explosion of ship, final score; Space/R restarts instantly, auto-restart after 6 s keeps attract mode alive.
- **Waves**: spawn interval, asteroid speed, and count ramp with elapsed time/score; brief "WAVE n" banner.

## 6. Autopilot AI (simple, robust)
Each frame: pick target = nearest asteroid weighted by z-distance (prioritize ones closing in); compute desired lateral velocity to align target's predicted position with the firing axis (lead the target using its velocity); add separation force from nearby asteroids to dodge; fire when |aim error| < threshold and cooldown ready; clamp to bounds. Result: competent, human-looking play for the demo.

## 7. Robustness / performance
- Pooling for bullets, asteroids, particles; shared geometries/materials; `dispose()` only for per-asteroid displaced geometry.
- `dt` clamped (avoid spiral after tab switch), `devicePixelRatio` capped at 2, resize handler, `visibilitychange` pauses.
- Single `requestAnimationFrame` loop; fixed-order update (input → state → AI → entities → collisions → particles → HUD → render).

## 8. Verification
1. `node --check` on the extracted inline JS (syntax).
2. Serve via `python3 -m http.server` and load in **headless Chromium**, capture console errors + a screenshot after 2 s (expect attract-mode gameplay visible) and after synthetic key events (expect manual control/sound context init).
3. Manual review of the idle-3s autopilot transition and restart flow in code.
